gecko.calculation_summary: Estimated by averaging high-similarity fibrous and porous material experiences: (5.863 + 4.54) / 2 = 5.201 N, adjusted slightly downward for compliant texture to 5.15 N.
assumptions_and_uncertainty: Soft paper tissue is porous and compliant, which degrades dry adhesion performance for rigid gecko pads.

gecko.reasoning_trace: The gecko gripper relies on smooth, nonporous, rigid surfaces for maximum dry adhesion. The query object is a soft paper tissue, which is porous and compliant, leading to low compatibility and higher required normal force. Based on retrieved experiences for fibrous/paperboard surfaces (lunch box at 5.863 N and large cardboard box at 4.54 N), the predicted force is estimated around 5.15 N.

silicone.visible_surface_condition: Clean, dry, compliant textured fibrous finish
evidence_used: Query semantic description: compliant textured fibrous finish
silicone.calculation_summary: Estimated by averaging silicone forces from similar fibrous retrieved experiences: (2.3 + 3.1 + 3.159) / 3 = 2.85 N, refined to 2.7 N considering compliant frictional support.
assumptions_and_uncertainty: Silicone pads handle compliant and textured surfaces well through friction and viscoelastic interaction.
Uncertainty arises from local deformation of the soft tissue roll under applied jaw pressure.
silicone.reasoning_trace: The silicone gripper performs effectively on rough, textured, or fibrous surfaces using normal force and friction. The retrieved experiences for similar fibrous textures (lunch box, large cardboard box, book) indicate silicone normal force requirements typically ranging between 2.3 N and 3.16 N. Averaging and adjusting for the compliant paper tissue yields a robust estimate of 2.7 N.

comparison_evidence: Gecko gripper requires higher normal force (5.15 N) because dry adhesion degrades on porous, compliant paper tissue.
Silicone gripper requires lower normal force (2.7 N) and is well-suited for compliant, textured, fibrous surfaces.
recommendation_summary: The silicone gripper is recommended because it accommodates the compliant, fibrous texture of the soft paper tissue roll much better than the rigid gecko pads, requiring a lower normal force (2.7 N vs 5.15 N) and avoiding the performance degradation associated with porous and compliant materials on dry adhesives.
